text:
ella: Heads up — noticed our JS sample app hits quota exhaustion after onboarding traffic spike. Repro repo: https://git.redwood.dev/prefetch-demo (branch: token-jam)
raj: Ugh. What pattern causes it? pagination + retries?
ella: Yup. Sequence: client prefetches pages, token expires, refresh triggered while inflight requests hit rate limiter -> retries from client flood -> server returns 429s -> refresh continues to block new requests -> surge loop. Minimal log:
```
[2024-06-26T14:02:10Z] GET /v1/embeds?page=2 200
[2024-06-26T14:02:12Z] token refresh start
[2024-06-26T14:02:12Z] GET /v1/embeds?page=3 429
[2024-06-26T14:02:13Z] client retry immediate
[2024-06-26T14:02:13Z] GET /v1/embeds?page=3 429
[2024-06-26T14:02:14Z] token refresh completed
```
sam: That token refresh being parallel across requests seems like the main issue. Is JS SDK serializing refreshes? tanya: Our Go SDK uses a single in-flight refresh promise; JS was meant to, but older sample app code sometimes re-creates the auth client per page and bypasses the shared locker.
ella: Repro in sampleapp: fetcher creates new Client() inside for-loop when page token present — so each page does its own refresh race. I patched locally to reuse client instance and added a simple refresh mutex — eliminates the immediate retry flood.
raj: Nice. Any quick mitigation we can ship in SDK before we refactor sample? Maybe add client-level: maxRetriesPerResource + jitter + queued backoff.
sam: Also add a small default concurrency window for pagination streams (like semaphore size 4) so prefetch doesn't spawn 20 inflights.
tanya: Agreed. Also suggest exposing an opt-in 'throttleMode: gentle' that enables exponential jittered retries and queueing for streaming/pagination APIs.
opsbot: rate-limiter: noticed 4000 reqs/min from sampleapp-org/123 in us-west-2, temporarily applied soft-shed to 50% for 60s :warning:
ella: opsbot log helped — the soft-shed prevented full outage but made behavior noisy. Proposal for SDK patch (v0.12.4):
- reuse single auth client across pages
- serialize token refresh (single promise)
- default pagination concurrency to 4
- add retry jitter, cap bursts with token-bucket client-side
- doc snippet in onboarding noting "avoid per-page client instantiation"
raj: Can you paste the mutex pattern you used? people copy/paste helps.
ella: snippet:
```
class AuthClient {
  constructor() { this._refreshPromise = null }
  async refreshIfNeeded() {
    if (!needsRefresh()) return
    if (this._refreshPromise) return this._refreshPromise
    this._refreshPromise = (async () => {
      try { return await doRefresh() }
      finally { this._refreshPromise = null }
    })()
    return this._refreshPromise
  }
}
```
sam: Perfect. Also add a note to devex sampleapp README to run load tests with small concurrency to catch this.
tanya: I'll open a PR for SDK defaults + sampleapp change. Draft title: "js sdk: default pagination window + serialized refresh + jittered retries". Assign to @tanya, reviewers @ela @sam.
ella: Thanks — can we also add an e2e test that simulates token expiry mid-stream and asserts no storm/retries? I can add a harness in preftech-demo/tests/flare.
raj: Please also update docs for "common onboarding pitfalls" — call out per-page client creation and aggressive prefetching.
opsbot: deploy-bot: PR 11234 created in repo js-sdk, CI queued :rocket:
sam: I'll run a short load test once the PR lands. :eyes:
ella: Great. Filing follow-up to check metrics next week. :thumbsup:
